conceptual assets.information: The stored enable setting controls whether the timer counts and generates interrupts, and it directly drives the clock-generator enable output. Timer operation and the downstream clock enable depend on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: an access can overwrite the enable bit at line 76; Availability: clearing it disables counting and interrupt generation at lines 118 and 141 and drives clkgen_en_o low through line 106.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could clear or set the enable bit, disabling the timer and its clock-generator output or causing operation when it should be disabled.

conceptual assets.information: The three-bit prescaler setting selects which clock-generator bit becomes the timer tick. The timer rate depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: bus writes can change the stored prescaler bits at lines 77-79; Availability: the selected clock-generator bit controls timer advancement through lines 117 and 120, so a setting selecting no effective tick can stop the timer.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could select an unsuitable or inactive clock-generator bit, changing the timer rate or preventing timer progress.

conceptual assets.information: The stored threshold is the timer count value at which an expiration match occurs. Timer rollover and interrupt generation depend on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus write replaces timer.thres at line 84; Availability: the threshold comparison at line 131 controls count reset at lines 121-123 and interrupt assertion at lines 142-143, so changing it can suppress or disrupt timer expiration.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could replace the threshold with a value that delays, suppresses or excessively accelerates timer expiration.

conceptual assets.information: The timer count is the elapsed-count state used to determine expiration and is incremented or cleared as the timer runs. It is returned by timer-count register reads.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: timer.count is reset, cleared and incremented by the state assignments at lines 115, 119, 122 and 124, so tampering can corrupt expiration behavior; Availability: timer progress and expiration depend on this state at lines 120-124 and it is observable in the readback at line 98.
conceptual assets.attack: A fault or unauthorized state modification could reset, freeze or corrupt the count, causing missed or incorrectly timed timer events.

conceptual assets.information: The expiration decision is the comparison of the current count with the stored threshold. It controls count rollover and interrupt assertion; it has no entry or exit port because it is computed internally and only used as a decision.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the comparison result at line 131 decides whether the count resets and whether an interrupt becomes pending at lines 121-123 and 142-143; Availability: forcing or suppressing this decision can prevent timer rollover or interrupt delivery.
conceptual assets.attack: Tampering with the comparison or its operands could force repeated expiration, prevent expiration, or generate an interrupt at the wrong time.

conceptual assets.information: The pending-interrupt state records that the timer has expired and remains asserted until cleared or the timer is disabled. It drives the interrupt output and is available through status readback.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: irq_pnd can be set, cleared or suppressed by the logic at lines 143, 145 and 148, and an incorrect value changes both interrupt reporting and readback; Availability: clearing or withholding irq_pnd can prevent irq_o from signaling the required timer event through line 154.

considered, not kept.reason: The address, read/write direction and strobe only qualify or select accesses to local registers, so Access command fields treats them as part of the accesses rather than as separate information.

The response data carries the kept register values, while ack repeats the request strobe and err is tied to a constant at lines 68-70, so the transfer record and handshake-copy rules give these no independent concept.
clkgen_i is sampled into timer.tick at line 117 and timer.tick only paces count advancement at line 120, so the Pacing pulses rule folds it into timer operation.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the internal assignments in lines 59-66, 111-116 and 136-140, and the Clocks and resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
